title: The Amendment Charge Owed on a Vacation Package
content:
The amendment charge owed on a vacation package answers a change the operations desk has already approved against that package, and it is entered against the party as a whole. This sheet records how the packages pricing team arrives at the figure on a package sold under any of Wanderlane's Vacation Package Products.

## The quantities that enter the figure

| Quantity | Where it is read from |
| --- | --- |
| The travellers on the package | the adults and the children the package records as travelling, taken together |
| The product's administration charge | the administration charge per traveller recorded against the product the package was booked under |

## The figure

The amendment charge's starting amount is the product's administration charge, read against every traveller on the package: the administration charge per traveller multiplied by the travellers on the package.

## The order in which the figures act

The starting amount and anything added to it are summed before the multiple is taken, the multiple acts once on that sum and never on either figure alone, and the payable share acts last, on the figure the multiple produced.

The amendment charge payable is that starting amount taken once and in full, rounded half up to the nearest cent at the end and at no earlier point. The rounding is applied to the completed figure; no part of the working is rounded before it.

## Worked on hypothetical particulars

A package recording 2 adults and 1 child travelling carries 3 travellers on it. On a product whose administration charge is 40.00 USD per traveller, the starting amount is 120.00 USD, and the amendment charge payable, that starting amount taken once and in full, is 120.00 USD.

A package recording 2 adults and no child travelling carries 2 travellers. On a product whose administration charge is 35.00 USD per traveller the amendment charge payable is 70.00 USD.

Where the multiplication produces a fraction of a cent — 3 travellers at 33.335 USD, say — the figure is carried at its full precision through the working and rounded half up to the nearest cent only once the figure is complete, giving 100.01 USD.
